responsibility: Provides rustc’s bridge from typed HIR to executable compiler middle IR by constructing and validating THIR, enforcing pre-MIR safety rules, lowering validated bodies into MIR, and running selected MIR-based analyses. The crate entry point in `lib.rs` wires this functionality into compiler queries and hooks, including THIR construction, match checking, unsafety checking, constant literal lowering, MIR building, and THIR debug printing. The `thir` module builds the Typed High-level IR for each body from typed HIR, preserving typing, scope, adjustments, unsafe context, literals, and user type annotations, and also performs pattern lowering and analysis such as deconstruction, usefulness/exhaustiveness, reachability, and irrefutability checking. The `check_unsafety.rs` root file walks THIR before MIR construction to ensure operations that require `unsafe` occur only in valid safety contexts, applying edition- and target-feature-specific rules and issuing diagnostics and lints. The `build` module then lowers THIR for functions, consts, and `custom_mir` inputs into well-formed MIR, coordinating CFG construction, scope and drop handling, expression and statement lowering, pattern-test and match-driven control flow, and parsing of the custom MIR DSL when present. Finally, `lints.rs` analyzes finished MIR control-flow graphs to emit MIR-based diagnostics, especially unconditional recursion and recursive `Drop` implementations. Together, these pieces make `rustc_mir_build` the compiler crate responsible for turning typed Rust bodies into checked MIR while preserving semantic information and enforcing safety and pattern-matching correctness.
